# Abdulmalik / saintmalik blog
> AppSec, DevSecOps, Kubernetes, and supply-chain notes from lived infra work.

Site: https://blog.saintmalik.me
Author: Abdulmalik (AppSec Engineer) - https://saintmalik.me

## Priority posts
- [MicroVM runners protect the host. Your supply chain still runs inside the job.](https://blog.saintmalik.me/ephemeral-microvm-runners-supply-chain/): Ephemeral microVM runners isolate the host from the job. Most CI supply-chain attacks still happen inside the job. What microVMs buy, what they miss, and where to spend first.
- [MCP this, MCP that. Attack surface, gateways, and cMCP.](https://blog.saintmalik.me/mcp-security-gateways-cmcp/): An MCP security gateway sits between the agent and tools/call: policy deny, audit trail, optional TEE. Walk cMCP Cedar against Cursor shaped filesystem MCP.
- [Vault control plane via GitOps. Secret values stay out of git.](https://blog.saintmalik.me/vault-gitops-control-plane/): Most of Vault on Kubernetes can be declared in git: HA, TLS, engines, policies, K8s auth, injector, snapshots. Terraform owns seal identity. Secret values and first init stay out o
- [Runtime Trace attestation: signed image, dishonest process](https://blog.saintmalik.me/runtime-trace-process-attestation/): Artifact signatures prove who sealed the digests. They do not prove what the build did. Runtime Trace is process attestation: observe the job, attach the predicate, gate promote on
- [Think EDR, but for CI/CD: cicd-sensor on GitHub Actions](https://blog.saintmalik.me/cicd-sensor-github-actions/): Artifact signing and pinned SHAs do not tell you what the job did. cicd-sensor is open-source runtime security for CI — EDR-shaped coverage for GitHub Actions and GitLab. This guid
- [Your JetStream is fine. You just have two of them.](https://blog.saintmalik.me/nats-jetstream-wrong-cluster/): Publisher acks, consumer never sees the message. Restart flushes a stuck queue. Realtime fan-out works on one pod and vanishes on another. Two JetStream stores behind one Service n
- [Eradicate long-lived tokens before they eradicate you](https://blog.saintmalik.me/eradicate-long-lived-tokens/): Long-lived GitHub PATs are a culture failure, not a tooling miss. What a multi-environment PAT campaign illustrated, and the short-lived App token patterns I use in CI so classic P
- [MongoDB Passwordless Authentication on Azure AKS using Workload Identity](https://blog.saintmalik.me/mongodb-passwordless-auth-aks/)
- [Do you know the supply chain risk your Helm charts carry?](https://blog.saintmalik.me/helm-gitops-supply-chain-checks/): Most teams scan app images in CI and ignore the Helm charts GitOps syncs. That is a real supply-chain blind spot. Render what would land, inventory the images, Syft + Grype fixable
- [Self-hosted Karpenter on AKS: Cilium, CAS, and the quota wall](https://blog.saintmalik.me/aks-karpenter-quota-constraints/): Why you cannot just flip the NAP addon on a Calico + CAS cluster, what Cilium costs you, and how regional vCPU quota turns NodePool requirements into filtered out all available ins
- [AKS + Karpenter: kubectl logs returns 401 Unauthorized](https://blog.saintmalik.me/aks-karpenter-kubectl-logs-401/): get/describe work, logs and exec return 401, but only on Karpenter nodes. RBAC-off AKS, kubelet anonymous-auth mismatch, and the DaemonSet that fixed it.
- [The Incident Response Step Most Teams Skip: Memory Forensics for Kubernetes](https://blog.saintmalik.me/kubernetes-memory-forensics-volatility/): Audit logs and Falco catch a lot. Fileless malware, process hollowing, and other in-memory artifacts often live only in RAM. How to capture worker-node memory with AVML and what Vo
- [Container Image SBOM Blind Spots: What Scanning Your Image Still Misses](https://blog.saintmalik.me/container-image-sbom-blind-spots/): An SBOM of your container image is not the SBOM of your app. Knowing which part is which, whether the bad code can run, and proving the image is the one you built all get harder on
- [GitHub Actions Supply Chain Attacks: How to Actually Harden Your CI/CD Pipeline](https://blog.saintmalik.me/github-actions-supply-chain-hardening/): Pinned SHAs and zizmor are not enough. After tj-actions and NX, here is how to phase static hardening, runtime egress control, and syscall visibility into a CI/CD supply chain prog
- [Kubernetes Runtime Security: The Silence That Should Keep You Up at Night](https://blog.saintmalik.me/kubernetes-runtime-security/): Two real assessments where attackers moved inside Kubernetes with zero alerts. A practical Falco setup with modern eBPF, custom rules, Falcosidekick, Talon, and EKS audit detection

- [Building a Kubernetes IR Playbook: Audit Logs Alone Wont Save You](https://blog.saintmalik.me/kube-ir-playbook-audit-logs/): Building a Kubernetes IR playbook from real EKS work. Why audit logs alone are not enough, why offline TSV sweeps beat ad-hoc jq at volume, and how lnav fits once the columns are f
- [SBOM Generation Is Not Enough: What to Actually Do With It](https://blog.saintmalik.me/sbom-supply-chain-beyond-generation/): Generating an SBOM is table stakes. The real question is what you do with it - querying for CVEs, license violations, and dependency age before they become incidents.
- [Zero Trust Network Access vs VPN: The Art of the Rabona](https://blog.saintmalik.me/vpn-vs-ztna-art-of-the-rabona/): WireGuard and OpenVPN get you inside the network. Zero Trust keeps you at the door of each app. Here is how I pick between them, and why teams under 50 often just reach for cloudfl
- [AWS Cloud Costs Nightmare, Cutting It To Elongate That Startup Runway](https://blog.saintmalik.me/cutting-aws-cloud-costs-for-startups/): Not generating revenue yet burning too much on cloud costs? Learn practical architectural and infrastructure strategies to cut your AWS bill and make that runway longer.
- [Cloudflare Access for Workers: protect internal apps without a VPN](https://blog.saintmalik.me/cloudflare-access-workers-for-internal-apps/): Put Cloudflare Access in front of Workers so internal dashboards need login first. Terraform for Access apps, IdP, and policies without a VPN.
- [Self-Healing HashiCorp Vault on Kubernetes: Helmization & Auto-Restore](https://blog.saintmalik.me/vault-self-healing-kubernetes/): Moving Vault to a GitOps flow is great, but what happens when you lose your data? Learn how to build a self-healing Vault cluster that restores itself from S3.
- [Ephemeral Resources and the End of Secrets in State Files](https://blog.saintmalik.me/opentofu-ephemeral-resources/): OpenTofu 1.11 introduces ephemeral resources that keep secrets out of state files forever. Learn about this game-changing feature.
- [Manage Helm secrets in ArgoCD without plaintext in Git](https://blog.saintmalik.me/helm-argocd-secret-management/): Dynamic secret injection for Helm charts deployed by ArgoCD. Companion to the ArgoCD Terraform install and multi-cluster posts.

Sibling posts cover Cosign key-based and Cosign keyless OIDC.
- [Enhanced IaC Security with State File Encryption Using OpenTofu](https://blog.saintmalik.me/iac-security-with-state-file-encryption/): Learn how to encrypt your OpenTofu state files using AWS KMS, GCP KMS, or PBKDF2. A practical guide for DevOps engineers looking to secure their infrastructure code.
